subject: ShieldPoint - evidence exchange & GRC integration playbook
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina@shieldpointsec.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: sec-ops@shieldpointsec.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + proposed evidence exchange workflow for Redwood integration

Hi Jordan and Vivek,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — we're excited about the integration between ShieldPoint GRC and Redwood. To move the SOC2 evidence sync and attestation automation forward, I've attached a draft scope and a short playbook that lays out how we exchange evidence, map controls, and handle access for on-prem customers.

High-level proposal:
- ShieldPoint will push control mappings via our integration webhook and provide an SFTP/secure-API endpoint for bulk evidence ingestion.
- For ad-hoc requests (customer audits, procurers), we can create time-limited evidence bundles and notify your CS/Legal teams.
- We recommend a joint runbook for pen test evidence ingestion so you can map test artifacts to Redwood controls without manual rework.

Attachments: shieldpoint-scope-v1.pdf (scope), evidence-exchange-instructions.docx (workflow).

Can we align on ownership for the transfer process? Suggest: Vivek for security sign-off, Jordan for partner ops, and Grace for customer success handoffs. If that looks good I can schedule a short sync early next week.

Thanks,
Lina Torres
Head of Integrations | ShieldPoint Security
Office: +1 415 555 0182

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina@shieldpointsec.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + proposed evidence exchange workflow for Redwood integration

Lina — thanks for sending this over and for the clear playbook.

Quick answers: yes to the proposed owners. A few asks from our side before we sync:
- Can you confirm that the SFTP endpoint supports transfer resume and checksums? We need reliable re-ingest for large artifact bundles.
- For the API option, we prefer OAuth2 client credentials with granular scopes rather than long-lived keys.
- Please highlight any data retention windows you expect for retained artifacts (ShieldPoint side).

I'll loop in Dylan from Platform Security (cc'd) to validate the transport/security detail. Grace — FYI on the customer success mapping; we'll want a short template for how we present the evidence bundle to customers during renewals.

If you can provision a read-only sample bundle with a trimmed dataset, we can validate ingestion this week. After that let's do a 30m technical handoff with our infra team.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Partner Ops | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0123

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina@shieldpointsec.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + proposed evidence exchange workflow for Redwood integration

Jordan / Vivek — quick security notes on the proposed approaches:
- SFTP: acceptable if we enforce server-host-key pinning, enforce chrooted accounts per partner, and require file-level SHA256 checksums.
- API: client_credentials + MTLS would be our preferred path for automated bulk ingestion. If ShieldPoint cannot support MTLS, OAuth2 + scoped JWTs is OK with short TTLs.
- Retention: we need retention metadata on every artifact so we can auto-purge after customer retention windows. Also require a signed manifest for any pen test artifacts to preserve chain-of-custody.

If ShieldPoint can provide a sample bundle (manifest + 3 artifacts) and a sandbox API credential, I'll run an end-to-end ingest test on our side.

—Dylan
Platform Security Engineer

From: Lina Torres <lina@shieldpointsec.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: sec-ops@shieldpointsec.com
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 07:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + proposed evidence exchange workflow for Redwood integration

Thanks Dylan — all good calls. We've provisioned a sandbox SFTP and a sandbox API for Redwood with the following:
- SFTP: sftp.redwood-sandbox@shieldpoint-sftp.shieldpointsec.com (resumes + SHA256 enforced)
- API: OAuth2 client credentials already created; MTLS planned for next sprint; we can give short-lived tokens while MTLS is in flight.
- Attached a small sample bundle (manifest + 3 artifacts) under the folder /samples/redwood-test.

Also attached: scp-integration-mapping.csv which maps our control IDs to Redwood control names. Retention metadata is embedded in the manifest.

Let us know a couple of windows when your infra/security folks can attempt a consume test. I'll be available Wed/Thu morning PT.

Lina

Attachments: scp-integration-mapping.csv

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina@shieldpointsec.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + proposed evidence exchange workflow for Redwood integration

Perfect — thanks. We'll run an ingest test Wednesday 10:30 AM PT. Goal: verify manifest parsing, checksum validation, and retention flags flow into our evidence store/CS dashboard.

Grace — can you prepare the customer-facing template as discussed? Keep it to one page: what we received, what we archived, and any customer-facing notes (retention, redaction).

Lina — please send the sandbox credentials to Dylan via the secure channel (do not include them on email). We'll confirm once the automated job completes.

If all passes, next steps:
- Create a short SLA addendum for evidence transfer timings (ShieldPoint -> Redwood).
- Define escalation path for missing artifacts during audits.
- Tentatively schedule a rollout to one pilot customer in April.

Thanks all,
Jordan

From: Lina Torres <lina@shieldpointsec.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + proposed evidence exchange workflow for Redwood integration

Dylan — sandbox credentials sent over the secure vault (we used the RedLock integration). You should see a request ticket ID: SP-REQ-4321 in the portal.

Let me know when your job runs and if any manifest fields need tweaks — we can update the mapping CSV easily.

Looking forward to the test.

Best,
Lina
ShieldPoint Security
